answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a grafted-orchard trust graph. A new identity starts with no reach: a sponsor must graft it onto the orchard by staking its own standing. Standing grows only when established peers echo an agent's work, each echo weighted by the echoing peer's standing. A Sybil cluster can echo itself forever, but those echoes carry no weight without links to the established orchard, so it can never reach the summit of trust for high-value jobs. Faking one credible identity means buying real service history, so cost scales with every fake.
